title: Performance and Physiological Effects of Race Pace-Based Versus Heart Rate Variability-Guided Training Prescription in Runners
authors: Ranieri LE, Casado A, Martin D, Trujillo-Colmena D, Gil-Arias A, Kenneally M, Jiménez A
findings: 28 runners were randomised to heart rate-based (n = 9), race pace-based (n = 9) or HRV-based (n = 10) prescription for 6 weeks.
No group x time interaction effects; main time effects for VO2max, running economy, sVT1, sVT2 and 7-km time trial (P < 0.001, 0.88 <= d <= 2.67).
The race-pace group improved the time trial (P < 0.05, ES = 1.07); the HRV group increased sVT2 (P < 0.01, ES = 1.34) and was more successful in boosting sVT1 and VO2max, but fat mass increased.
Lowest inter-individual variation in time trial in the race-pace group (CV = 0.82); HRV group had lower variation in relative VO2max (0.75) and sVT2 (0.79).
Training load was similar between groups (P > 0.05) and all groups followed a pyramidal intensity distribution.
limitations: Groups of 9-10 and 6 weeks; no between-group interaction effects, so group differences are descriptive and rest on within-group changes.
implications: Most recent runner-specific RCT shows no between-group advantage for HRV-guided over HR-based or race-pace-based prescription at equal load, so HRV should not replace pace/HR zones as the intensity anchor.
Keep pace/HR-based zone prescription as the core and use HRV as a modifier only.
No change to intensity distribution is justified by HRV evidence.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, MSSE, first author Ranieri, 12 Feb 2025. Numbers verified in the raw Europe PMC abstract (PMID 39935030). First-author initials corrected to Ranieri LE. Downgraded evidence level B to C (n = 28, 9-10 per arm).
